question: Does answering multiple choice as (choice)(why) preserve accuracy? PHASE 1 GATE.
model: lingshu-medical-mllm/Lingshu-7B (cheap leg), greedy temperature=0, tp=1, fullres, max_tokens=320 for EVERY arm

system_by_arm.A_letter_only: Answer with only the correct option letter (e.g. 'A'). Do not explain.
system_by_arm.B_answer_first: Answer with the correct option letter first (e.g. 'A'), then explain in one or two short sentences why that option is correct. Example: "A. The mass is in the left lower lobe."
system_by_arm.C_reason_first: Explain in one or two short sentences why an option is correct, then answer with the correct option letter last (e.g. 'A'). Example: "The mass is in the left lower lobe. A."
system_by_arm.B2_answer_first_forced: Answer with the correct option letter first (e.g. 'A'), then, in exactly one sentence, state the specific finding in the image that makes that option correct. Always give the sentence, even when the answer is obvious. Example: "A. The mass is in the left lower lobe."
system_by_arm.C2_reason_first_forced: First, in exactly one sentence, state the specific finding in the image that makes an option correct, then answer with that option letter last (e.g. 'A'). Always give the sentence, even when the answer is obvious. Example: "The mass is in the left lower lobe. A."

gate.rule: go=true iff the best (choice)(why) arm loses <= ~0.02 accuracy vs letter-only (or gains) AND its rationales look discriminative

criterion_1_accuracy.verdict: PASS -- decisively; the format is free, slightly positive
criterion_1_accuracy.note: no benchmark shows a significant loss; parse_ok is 1.000 so no arm is silently randomised; the arm-A null test reproduces the repo's existing Lingshu-7B MCQ dump.

criterion_2_discriminative.verdict: PASS with a caveat -- the rationales are gradeable text and create real candidate diversity, but the cheap text-only proxy adds ~0 over the deployed letter-margin

candidates_a_selector_can_act_on.interpretation: this is the hypothesised mechanism, measured: each competing option now arrives with ~2.7 textually distinct justifications instead of ~1.6 near-identical letter strings, and there is +0.44 of oracle headroom above self-consistency to select into.

caveats: 42% of B2 answers still carry NO justification (<3 words beyond restating the option); on those items best-of-N degenerates exactly as it does today.

within a benchmark, a cross-fitted TF-IDF probe on the justification alone reaches AUROC 0.46-0.73 and adds -0.03..+0.05 over the letter-margin confidence the deployed gate already uses -- so the rationale is NOT obviously incremental to a POINTWISE correctness score. Its value is expected to be in BETWEEN-CANDIDATE discrimination, which this greedy pilot cannot measure and Phase 2 must.
the pooled TF-IDF AUROC of 0.72-0.75 is INFLATED by benchmark identity (per-benchmark accuracy spans 0.26-0.85) and must not be cited.
under sampling (temp 0.7) B2 self-consistency@8 is 0.668 vs 0.690 for letter-only on SLAKE+PMC-VQA -- a 0.022 deficit that a verifier must clear before showing net gain.

ordering_control_finding1.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE as a mechanism test; INTENT-TO-TREAT result is consistent with Finding 1
ordering_control_finding1.arm_C_failed: arm C never complied (letter_first_rate 1.000, 0.0 justification words) -- it is NOT a chain-of-thought control and its numbers say nothing about ordering
ordering_control_finding1.arm_C2_partial: arm C2 forced the sentence but Lingshu-7B still answered letter-first on ~90% of items; only ~10% genuinely reasoned first
ordering_control_finding1.reading: the reason-first INSTRUCTION costs accuracy on the perception benchmarks (C2-A = -0.024 [-0.040,-0.008]) while the answer-first instruction is free (B2-A = 0.000 [-0.014,+0.014]); B2-C2 = +0.024 [+0.010,+0.038]. This is the direction Finding 1 predicts. But because C2 complied on only ~10% of items this is an intent-to-treat effect of the instruction, NOT a clean test of answer-vs-reason ordering. On the self-selected compliant subset C2 vs A is +0.014 [-0.043,+0.071] (n=140).

what_phase_2_must_show_before_anything_i: that a verifier scoring (choice)(why) candidates beats BOTH self-consistency@8 AND the existing letter-margin gate on the letter-disagreement items -- the pointwise proxy here does not guarantee it
an image-disjoint split asserted on md5 of DECODED RGB pixels (the manifest at ckpts/choicewhy_pilot/items.jsonl already records these)
composition-matched training data vs any comparator

reason_first_instruction_following_audit.verdict: arm C DID NOT follow its instruction (letter_first_rate 1.000, zero justification words) so arm C is NOT a chain-of-thought control; arm C2, which forces the sentence, is the control that actually ran.

C_reason_first.note: the two extraction rules are compared so that a reason-first arm's reported accuracy cannot be an artifact of assuming the letter is last.

C2_reason_first_forced.note: the two extraction rules are compared so that a reason-first arm's reported accuracy cannot be an artifact of assuming the letter is last.

degenerate_rationale.definition: text remaining after removing the leading answer letter AND a verbatim restatement of the chosen option; <3 words = the model restated the option and justified nothing

discriminativeness_within_benchmark.why: the pooled TF-IDF AUROC is confounded by benchmark identity (per-benchmark accuracy ranges 0.26-0.85), so a text model can score well by merely recognising which benchmark an item is from. These are the honest per-benchmark numbers, plus whether the rationale adds anything ON TOP of the letter-margin confidence the deployed gate already uses.

signals.margin: exp(top1 logprob) - exp(top2 logprob) at the answer-letter position
signals.text: TF-IDF(1,2)-grams of the justification only (option restatement removed), 5-fold cross-fitted logistic regression
signals.note_arm_A: arm A has no justification; its 'text' column is a floor/sanity control

decode_token_cost.note: MEASURED decode tokens only. Total FLOPs are prefill-dominated for a VLM (image tokens), so this ratio is an upper bound on the relative cost increase, not the cost increase itself.

a_C2_on_items_it_actually_reasoned_first.selection: items where C2 put the letter LAST and wrote >=3 words of justification
a_C2_on_items_it_actually_reasoned_first.CAVEAT: SELF-SELECTED subset -- the model chose when to reason first, and it reasons on the items it finds hard, so this comparison is descriptive, NOT a causal estimate of the ordering effect.

b_B2_on_items_it_actually_justified.selection: items where B2 wrote >=3 words of justification after the letter
b_B2_on_items_it_actually_justified.CAVEAT: self-selected in the same way; descriptive.

c_discriminativeness_restricted_to_items.why: the fair test of 'can a verifier grade this': only items that actually carry a justification, and does the text beat / add to the letter-margin confidence.

best_of_n_probe.question: does the (choice)(why) format change the best-of-N picture on MCQ, i.e. is there headroom for a verifier to select into, and are the candidates distinguishable?
best_of_n_probe.setup: N=8, temperature 0.7, seed 1234, same items and same prompts as the greedy arms; SLAKE-closed (416) + PMC-VQA (500) only

conditional_on_letter_disagreement.why: a selector can only change the answer on items where the 8 samples do not all give the same letter; ALL of the best-of-N headroom lives here. This is the population a verifier acts on.
